history.dynasty: Not documented (present marble-clad structure about a century old)
history.period: Ancient Shakti Peetha site; present structure circa early 20th century (approximate — flag)
history.summary: Fullara (Attahas) is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas: legend says Devi Sati's lower lip fell here as Shiva's Tandava body was dismembered by Vishnu's Sudarshan Chakra. There is no idol in the garbhagriha; a large vermilion-smeared stone (about 15-18 feet wide) is worshipped as the Devi. Bhairav Vishwesh sits on a lotus beside the temple. A big pond beside the temple is where, by hearsay, Hanuman gathered 108 blue lotuses for Rama's worship of Durga. One travel account puts the present temple at 'almost 100 years old' — an approximate, unverified claim. CSV town correction: the CSV gives 'Birbhum', which is the district; the temple-town of Fullara lies just east of Labhpur, so town is corrected to Fullara (near Labhpur).

name: Fullara Temple
town_description: Labhpur is a market town in the Bolpur subdivision of Birbhum district, West Bengal, about 30 km from Bolpur Shantiniketan. The Fullara temple-town lies just east of it amid red-soil fields and greenery, with the Kanuri river and a large temple pond nearby; the area is known for the Attahas Shakti Peetha, its annual Magh Purnima fair, and its literary associations.
